subject: probability-statistics
title: Descriptive statistics & moments
introduction: Summary statistics compress a dataset or distribution. The exam tests whether you know exactly what information survives that compression—and how location, scale, and dependence change under transformations.
theory: Mean is balance point, median is a quantile, and mode is peak frequency; they answer different questions. Variance measures squared spread around the mean.
Covariance captures linear co-movement and depends on units. Correlation standardizes it to $[-1,1]$ but zero correlation does not generally imply independence.

examples.title: Shift and scale
examples.solution: $E[Y]=10$ and $Var(Y)=9(5)=45$; shifts do not affect variance.

examples.title: Update a mean
examples.solution: The old sum is 40, so the new mean is $(40+14)/6=9$.

pitfalls: Letting an additive shift change variance.
Treating zero correlation as independence without extra assumptions.
Using population and sample variance denominators interchangeably.
Forgetting the second term in the law of total variance.
whyGate: These quantities drive standardization, regression, PCA covariance matrices, estimators, and uncertainty analysis.
